summary: The incident is narrowed to two verified auth-service change events that bracket an unambiguous step change at 14:00Z: the dep-5710 deploy (jjwt 0.11->0.12, TokenValidator rewrite) at 14:00:00Z and the cfg-2705 signing-key rotation (jwt.signing.key_id k-2025-10 -> k-2026-04) at 14:01:00Z. Onset, mechanism class and scope are well established: error_rate jumps from ~0.2% to a flat ~36% invalid_token plateau, served in-band at flat p99 (~90ms), flat request rate (~400 req/s), flat CPU/mem, zero restarts and unchanged rate-limiting, with blast radius confined to auth-service and shared-cache/capacity origins positively excluded. However, H1 (jjwt parser regression) and H2 (non-atomic key-id/JWKS propagation) cannot be separated: they have different fixes and each rests on an unverified mechanism hop, with confidence 0.50 vs 0.22 and a ranking that the Critic judged under-determined by precedent matching alone. Since every decisive discriminator (per-replica/AZ error rate, gateway 401 counters, pod-level JWKS/key-id logs, rollout/JWKS propagation metadata) is unavailable or unqueryable, I report inconclusive and treat H2 as a live alternative of comparable mechanistic weight rather than as a distant second.

ranked_hypotheses.title: JWT library 0.11→0.12 parser regression (dep-5710) rejects a token-shape subset
ranked_hypotheses.statement: auth-service v7.3.0 (dep-5710, live at 14:00:00Z) upgraded jjwt 0.11→0.12 — a documented breaking parser API change — and rewrote TokenValidator. The new parser rejects a stable subset of otherwise-valid tokens (changed claims/clock-skew defaults, as in HIST-109), giving the persistent ~36% invalid_token plateau. The scheduled key-id rotation one minute later is a same-window coincidence, not the cause.

causal_chain.claim: Deploy dep-5710 ships jjwt 0.12 (breaking parser API) + rewritten TokenValidator at 14:00:00Z; it is the only auth-service deployment that day and it precedes/straddles the first elevated 14:00Z bucket
The rewritten parser's changed defaults reject a stable subset of token shapes → invalid_token (no direct observation of a failing token-shape cluster exists; flagged as an evidence-free hop)
Error rate steps from ~0.20% to 22-38% in the 14:00Z bucket and holds a ~36% plateau through 15:52-15:59Z
Failures are in-band: flat ~400 req/s, flat ~90ms p99, flat ~38% CPU / ~52% mem, flat rate limiting → validation-logic fault, not load or shedding
The plateau is FLAT for ~2h (no decay), which is what a persistent code-path rejection produces and is in tension with a lagging key-load story that should decay
Partial 36% (not ~100%) failure ⇒ a subset of tokens/code paths rather than a total parser break
Upstream api-gateway callers surface the 401s to users as logged-out sessions

assumptions: jjwt 0.12's changed defaults reject roughly a third of tokens rather than all or none — this hop has no direct observation of a failing token-shape cluster.
No rollback has occurred, so the 36% plateau is read as the post-change steady state; there is no recovery signal to attribute.
The parser path is exercised for only the subset of tokens; the remainder bypass or survive it.
HIST-108 does not apply better than HIST-109 despite its higher retrieval match_score.

ranked_hypotheses.title: Scheduled signing-key rotation (cfg-2705) published the new key-id before all validators accepted it
ranked_hypotheses.statement: At 14:01:00Z 'security-automation' rotated jwt.signing.key_id k-2025-10 → k-2026-04. Per precedent HIST-108, the new key-id was published before all auth-service validators loaded the new JWKS, so not-yet-updated validators (or tokens minted under the retired key-id) reject ~36% of validations. The jjwt upgrade one minute earlier is a coincidental same-window deploy, not the cause.

causal_chain.claim: cfg-2705 rotates jwt.signing.key_id k-2025-10 → k-2026-04 at 14:01:00Z, a single atomic config record, one minute after the deploy

New key-id is published before all pods/validators load the new JWKS, so not-yet-updated validators reject the rotated-key tokens (assumed; the config record carries no distribution channel, JWKS artifact id or per-replica timestamps)
Error rate steps to ~36% in the 14:00Z bucket and holds the plateau
Rejections are in-band 401s at flat latency/traffic/CPU, i.e. key-id acceptance rather than overload
36%-not-100% subset matches the HIST-108 'new key id before all pods loaded the JWKS' shape, the highest-match precedent retrieved
Upstream api-gateway callers surface the 401s to users as logged-out sessions

assumptions: JWKS/key-id propagation to all replicas is non-atomic or slow — no rollout strategy, replica count or JWKS-propagation state was obtainable.
The rotation, not the same-minute deploy, is what flips key-id acceptance.

The 36% share corresponds to the not-yet-propagated share of validators or of old-key tokens, and that share has been stable for ~2h (required to fit the flat plateau, which a decaying propagation story does not explain).

ranked_hypotheses.title: Shared session/token cache (redis-cache) or user-db degrading caused subset 401s
ranked_hypotheses.statement: auth-service's shared dependency redis-cache (shared:true, also used by portfolio-service, pricing-engine, market-data-service) or its user-db may have degraded, so a subset of token/session lookups fail and are returned as invalid_token 401s, while auth-service's own code and config are healthy.

causal_chain.claim: redis-cache is shared across auth-service and portfolio-service/pricing-engine/market-data-service
Cache/session path degrades and a subset of lookups fail (assumed)
Failed lookups surface as invalid_token 401s at auth-service (assumed)
Error rate steps to a ~36% plateau at 14:00Z

ranked_hypotheses.rejection_reason: Positively excluded and now cross-consumer confirmed: no deployment or config change touched redis-cache, user-db, kyc-provider or api-gateway on 2026-04-15 (F16), the prior day had zero change events (F4), and the onset is a precise step at 14:00Z coinciding with two auth-service changes (F13). redis-cache health is flat across onset on all five exposed metrics — hit ratio ~95-97% (F25), connected_clients ~300-320 (F26), evictions ~3/min (F27), CPU ~22% (F28), memory ~66-72% (F29) — so no cache-side error, eviction or pool-saturation signal exists (F30). The stronger cross-consumer discriminator has now resolved FLAT: none of the three shared redis-cache co-tenants shows any error or latency step at 14:00Z (F42-F45, F47), which closes the shared-cache path. Retained as rejected; residual gap is only that redis-cache itself exposes no error_rate/latency metric (F30).

ranked_hypotheses.title: Capacity/resource exhaustion or traffic surge on auth-service
ranked_hypotheses.statement: A traffic surge, connection-pool exhaustion, thread/CPU saturation or rate limiting on auth-service caused ~36% of validations to fail with 401s.

causal_chain.claim: Traffic, CPU, memory or pools saturate at 14:00Z (assumed)
Saturation causes ~36% of validations to fail as invalid_token 401s (assumed)

ranked_hypotheses.rejection_reason: Directly contradicted by every resource and traffic signal: request_rate flat ~360-435 req/s across onset (F8, F23), latency_p99 flat ~90ms (F9), CPU flat ~38% / mem ~52% (F10), restarts = 0 (F11), rate_limited_per_min flat ~2/min (F12). The failure is an in-band step change at normal latency and normal load — the signature of a validation-logic/acceptance fault, not overload (F17).

facts.statement: Two auth-service change events bracket the 401 onset on 2026-04-15: deployment dep-5710 v7.3.0 at 14:00:00Z ('Upgrade JWT library to 4.x; refactor token validation'; changes 'jjwt 0.11 -> 0.12 (breaking parser API)' and 'TokenValidator rewritten') and, one minute later at 14:01:00Z, config change cfg-2705 setting jwt.signing.key_id from 'k-2025-10' to 'k-2026-04' by 'security-automation'.

auth-service error_rate was flat at ~0.2% until 13:52Z, then stepped to 27.92% avg (max 38.53%) in the 14:00:00Z bucket and held a ~36% plateau (e.g. 36.27, 35.79, 36.55, 36.31) through 15:52Z; the aggregate series is complete (missing_points 0) and the onset is a step, not a ramp.

The failure is in-band and not load-related: request_rate stayed ~380-410 req/s (mean 398.82, min 357.99, max 435.3), latency_p99 ~90ms, CPU ~38%, memory ~52%, rate_limited_per_min ~2/min, and restarts = 0 in every bucket across the window.

Blast radius and dependency scope: auth-service's only shared downstream component is redis-cache (shared:true, also used by portfolio-service, pricing-engine, market-data-service); user-db is shared:false and kyc-provider is external. No deployment or config change touched user-db, redis-cache, kyc-provider or api-gateway on 2026-04-15.

redis-cache health was flat across the 14:00Z onset on all five exposed metrics: hit ratio ~95-97%, connected_clients ~300-320, evictions ~3/min, CPU ~22%, memory ~66-72%; no cache-side error, eviction or saturation signal exists.

All three shared redis-cache co-tenants (portfolio-service, pricing-engine, market-data-service) were flat in error_rate (0.17-0.27% throughout) and latency (p99 ~180ms, ~60ms, ~40ms respectively) across the 14:00Z onset, closing the shared-cache propagation path.

Neither change has been reverted: dep-5710 status is 'live' with rolled_back_at null and no config change reverting cfg-2705 exists, so the ~36% plateau is a sustained post-change steady state with no recovery signal.

No per-replica, per-pod or per-AZ metric dimension exists: auth-service exposes only 7 aggregate metrics, and service ids 'auth-service-us-east-1a/b/c', 'auth-service-0' and 'auth-service-pod-1' all returned not_found.

api-gateway telemetry was unobtainable: its 401/invalid_token counters and error_rate could not be queried (the only telemetry path accepted auth-service), and get_deployments for api-gateway failed 503 on every attempt, so the shared final hop of both causal chains stays ungrounded.

Historical precedents with matching symptoms exist and point to the two change types seen today: HIST-108 (401s after JWT signing key rotation; new key-id published before all pods loaded the JWKS) and HIST-109 (token validation regression after JWT library upgrade; changed clock-skew default).

The 2026-04-14 baseline day had zero deployments and zero config changes, making the 2026-04-15 deploy+rotation pair an isolated change event; the identity-namespace log pipeline is down so auth-service logs were unavailable.

assumptions: ASSUMED: jjwt 0.12's changed parser/clock-skew defaults reject roughly one third of token shapes rather than all or none - there is no direct observation of a failing token-shape cluster (H1's mechanism hop is unverified).

ASSUMED: JWKS/key-id propagation to auth-service replicas is non-atomic or slow, so only some validators accepted k-2026-04; no replica count, rollout strategy or JWKS-propagation state was obtainable, and cfg-2705 appears as a single atomic scalar record with no distribution metadata (H2's mechanism hop is unverified).
ASSUMED: The 36% share is a stable steady state representative of the post-change failure subset, since no rollback has occurred and there is no recovery signal to attribute.

ASSUMED: The step onset is attributable to one or both of the two bracketing auth-service change events rather than to an unrecorded secret/KMS change, since no such change event is exposed by tooling.

ASSUMED: Precedent match weighting (HIST-108 key-rotation vs HIST-109 library-upgrade) is not sufficient to rank the two mechanisms; both precedents are leads, not evidence about the current incident (HIST-108 match_score 7.5/6 vs HIST-109 3.5/2, retrieval scoring is not mechanism evidence).

(demoted from facts: no verified observation backs it) The ~36% (not ~100%) partial-failure pattern is consistent with a subset mechanism for either change but does not discriminate between them: neither a global parser breakage nor a total key loss matches a stable one-third plateau.

timeline.event: Baseline day: no deployments and no config changes for any service (count 0) - the following day's change pair is an isolated event.
auth-service error_rate flat at ~0.2% (through 13:52Z); request_rate ~380-410 req/s, p99 ~90ms, CPU ~38%, mem ~52%, restarts 0.
market-data-service v5.0.3 deployed (~2.4h before onset); its own error_rate and latency remained flat through the incident window.
auth-service deployment dep-5710 v7.3.0 goes live: 'Upgrade JWT library to 4.x; refactor token validation', changes jjwt 0.11 -> 0.12 (breaking parser API) and TokenValidator rewritten.
Error-rate step: first elevated bucket, avg 27.92% (max 38.53%), then a ~36% plateau through 15:52Z; onset is a step change at the same bucket as the deploy.
Config change cfg-2705 by 'security-automation' rotates jwt.signing.key_id 'k-2025-10' -> 'k-2026-04' (Scheduled signing-key rotation); the only config change in the window.
No resource or traffic shift accompanies the step: request_rate ~401 req/s, p99 ~89.7ms, CPU ~39%, mem ~52.4%, rate_limited ~2.1/min.
redis-cache health flat across onset (hit ratio 96.17%, clients 310.5, evictions 3.26/min, CPU 21.7%, mem 70.07%); all three shared-cache co-tenants show no error or latency step.
Both changes still live with no rollback recorded (dep-5710 status 'live', rolled_back_at null; no reverting config change), and the ~36% plateau persists to the latest data.
Discriminating evidence remains unobtainable: no per-replica/AZ metric dimension, api-gateway 401 counters unqueryable, identity-namespace log pipeline down.

recommended_actions.action: Safe mitigation that does not pre-committing to either hypothesis: roll back dep-5710 (auth-service v7.3.0 -> previous version, i.e. revert jjwt 0.11/TokenValidator rewrite) AND in parallel re-point jwt.signing.key_id (cfg-2705) back to 'k-2025-10' with a staged re-publish; treating both changes as suspects is justified because H1 and H2 differ by only ~0.02-0.28 in confidence and have different fixes.
recommended_actions.rationale: Onset coincides exactly with these two auth-service changes (F1, F2, F13), both are still live with no rollback and no recovery signal (F3, F15), and the plateau has persisted ~2h at ~36% (F7, F22). Because the ranking is under-determined, a single-hypothesis rollback risks the wrong fix; reverting both removes the trigger while preserving the ability to re-introduce them one at a time.

recommended_actions.action: Discriminate before re-introducing any change: re-apply each change individually with a hold window and watch auth-service error_rate - first re-apply the jjwt 0.11->0.12 / TokenValidator change alone (without the key rotation) and observe whether the ~36% invalid_token plateau returns.
recommended_actions.rationale: The single most direct causal test available given that per-replica metrics and logs are unavailable (F19, F20, F21, F24, F37). A plateau reappearing on the parser change alone confirms H1 (dep-5710) and exonerates cfg-2705; nothing reappearing points to H2.

recommended_actions.action: Second discrimination leg: re-apply cfg-2705 key rotation alone (k-2026-04 published to all validators with the pre-0.12 code) and observe whether the plateau returns; additionally capture JWKS-load / key-id acceptance state per pod during the window.
recommended_actions.rationale: H2's mechanism hop (non-atomic JWKS/key-id propagation) has no direct observation and must be grounded empirically (F32, F31); a plateau returning on the rotation alone confirms H2 and exonerates the deploy.

recommended_actions.action: Instrument the missing discriminators permanently: add per-replica/per-pod/AZ labels to auth-service error_rate and add an explicit invalid_token reason code (key-id mismatch vs claims/clock-skew parse failure) to auth-service metrics or structured logs before any change is redeployed.
recommended_actions.rationale: The decisive subset-vs-global discriminator was unobtainable because the metric surface is aggregate-only (F19, F20, F21, F24); reason codes would have separated key-id-driven rejection from parser-driven rejection directly. This is the highest-value fix to make any future recurrence diagnosable in minutes.

recommended_actions.action: Expose rollout and JWKS-propagation metadata: record and surface replica count, rollout strategy (rolling/blue-green/staged), per-pod apply timestamps and the JWKS artifact/key-id version per replica for both deployments and config changes.
recommended_actions.rationale: dep-5710 and cfg-2705 records carry no replica count, rollout strategy or per-replica application timestamps (F31, F32), which is why the 36%-not-100% subset magnitude fits both stories (F18) and part (1)/(2) of the investigation could not be answered.

recommended_actions.action: Restore and harden the identity-namespace log pipeline (currently down since this morning) and alert on pipeline health, since its outage removed all pod-level invalid_token/key-id detail during a SEV-1.
recommended_actions.rationale: Logs would have provided the direct per-request rejection reason and pod identity needed to separate H1 from H2; their absence is explicitly noted in the incident report and forced the conclusion to inconclusive.

recommended_actions.action: Fix queryability of api-gateway telemetry and deployment API (currently 503 / restricted to auth-service) so the caller-side 401/session-invalidation series can be compared in lockstep with auth-service's step.
recommended_actions.rationale: The shared final hop of both causal chains ('callers surface 401s as logged-out sessions') stayed ungrounded because gateway metrics were unqueryable and get_deployments for api-gateway failed 503 (F37, F38, F41).

recommended_actions.action: Eliminate same-window change overlap: schedule signing-key rotations and auth-service library deploys in separate maintenance windows with a mandatory verification gap, and gate the key rotation behind a validator-capability check (all replicas report JWKS k-2026-04 loaded before the key-id is published).
recommended_actions.rationale: HIST-108 ('key rotation published new key id before all pods loaded the JWKS') and HIST-109 ('JWT library upgrade changed clock-skew default') both describe this failure class (F6, F36), and today's incident reproduced the exact overlap of a library-upgrade deploy and a key rotation one minute apart (F1, F2, F13).

recommended_actions.action: Add a pre-deploy compatibility test for auth-service token validation covering the production token-shape population (claim variants and clock-skew boundaries) plus a canary stage that halts rollout when invalid_token rate exceeds a threshold.
recommended_actions.rationale: A breaking parser API change (jjwt 0.11->0.12) was shipped straight into a step-change failure with no canary stop and no rollback for ~2h (F1, F3, F15); a token-shape compatibility gate and canary halt would have caught or contained the subset rejection before full rollout.

data_gaps: Per-replica/per-pod/per-AZ error rate is permanently unavailable: auth-service exposes only 7 aggregate metrics and no instance-level service id exists (F19, F20, F21, F24), so the subset-vs-uniform discriminator that would separate H2 (subset of replicas lacking the new key) from H1 (subset of token shapes hitting the changed parser) could not be measured.

api-gateway 401/invalid_token counters and error_rate for 13:00-15:59Z were never obtained (telemetry path accepted only auth-service), and get_deployments for api-gateway failed 503 on all attempts - so the caller-side lockstep comparison is missing (F37, F38, F41).

auth-service logs are unsearchable (identity-namespace log pipeline down since morning), so no per-request invalid_token reason code, key-id, or serving pod could be observed; onset is known only at metric-bucket resolution.

No rollout/JWKS-propagation metadata: dep-5710 and cfg-2705 records expose no replica count, rollout strategy, per-pod application timestamps, distribution channel, atomicity flag or JWKS artifact id (F31, F32), so the non-atomic-propagation mechanism of H2 remains untestable from change data.

redis-cache exposes no error_rate and no latency metric (only connected_clients, cpu_pct, evictions_per_min, hit_ratio_pct, memory_pct); its health is inferred from those five metrics and cross-consumer flatness (F25-F30, F42-F47).

No telemetry for user-db or kyc-provider around 14:00Z, and kyc-provider is external with has_telemetry:false; an unobserved shared-component contribution cannot be formally excluded, though user-db is shared:false and no change touched it (F16).

No KMS/secret-store change events are exposed by the config-change tool and only 2026-04-14 onward history was checked, so an earlier or out-of-band signing-key/secret change cannot be fully ruled out.

The first historical-incident search timed out and one subsequent attempt returned 503, so the precedent set (HIST-108/HIST-109) may be incomplete and additional key-rotation-during-rollout precedents may exist (F6, F36).
One re-query of auth-service cpu_pct failed with a retryable 503, so the CPU-flat reading could not be independently re-confirmed within the re-check window (F10).
what_would_change_the_conclusion: Per-replica or per-pod error_rate showing the ~36% failures concentrated on a stable subset of instances (not-yet-updated validators) would resolve toward H2 (cfg-2705 key rotation); an even spread across all replicas proportional to token shape would resolve toward H1 (dep-5710 parser).

Auth-service logs (or new reason-code metrics) showing the rejected tokens fail with a key-id/JWKS mismatch would confirm H2; failures on claims/clock-skew parse errors with valid key-id would confirm H1.

A canary or single-variable re-application test: if the ~36% plateau reappears when the jjwt 0.11->0.12 + TokenValidator change is re-applied alone, H1 is confirmed; if it reappears only when cfg-2705 key-id k-2026-04 is re-applied alone, H2 is confirmed.

api-gateway 401/session-invalidation counters rising in lockstep to ~36% at 14:00Z would confirm that the observed failures are the token-rejection path reaching callers, but would not by itself separate H1 from H2.
Evidence of an out-of-band KMS/secret-store or unrecorded key change (or a JWKS artifact publication failure) would open a third mechanism and could overturn both H1 and H2.
A recovery of the ~36% error rate without any rollback (self-healing propagation) would argue for a transient propagation fault (H2) rather than a persistent parser regression (H1).

Direct evidence that jjwt 0.12 cannot plausibly reject a stable ~1/3 subset of production token shapes (e.g. a documented, quantified incompatibility or a test corpus result) would downgrade H1 and promote H2.

findings.statement: The 401 onset is a step change that cannot be attributed to a redeploy/restart of pods at the moment of failure: T1 found restarts = 0.0 in every bucket 10:00-15:52Z, and only one auth-service deployment exists on 2026-04-15 (dep-5710 at 14:00:00Z), i.e. a single rollout event, with no second deploy or instance-level churn afterwards.

Neither change has been reverted as of the latest data: dep-5710 status is 'live' with rolled_back_at null, and cfg-2705 remains the only auth-service config change (no reverting change to jwt.signing.key_id). So there is no rollback marker correlating with any recovery in the 14:00-15:52Z plateau.

Blast radius is confined to auth-service's own token-validation path, not to any shared dependency: auth-service's only shared downstream component is redis-cache (shared:true, also used by portfolio-service, pricing-engine and market-data-service) plus user-db (postgres, shared:false) and kyc-provider (external, no telemetry). No deployment or config change touched user-db, redis-cache, kyc-provider or the upstream api-gateway on 2026-04-15, so a shared-component change cannot explain the 401s.

findings.statement: Because token rejection is in-band (401s served at flat ~90ms p99, flat ~400 req/s and flat CPU ~38%/mem ~52% per T1) and no resource or traffic signal moved, the failure shape is consistent with a token-VALIDATION logic change (library parser behaviour and/or key-id acceptance) rather than overloading, rate limiting or a neighbour hurting auth-service through a shared datastore/cache.

The ~36% (not ~100%) partial-failure pattern does NOT match a global total-fault shape for either change: a key-id rotation before all pods loaded the new key (HIST-108 precedent, match_score 7.5, 'Key rotation published new key id before all pods loaded the JWKS') would reject only tokens issued/signed under the old key-id by not-yet-updated validators, and a JWT-library parser regression (HIST-109, match_score 3.5) would reject only tokens hitting the changed code path - both are subset patterns. A uniform 100% breakage across every replica would be expected if the deploy had fully broken parsing for all tokens or if all pods had lost all keys at once; the observed steady 36% plateau instead fits a stable subset of replicas/pods not yet serving/accepting the new key or of token/claims shapes hitting the changed path.

findings.statement: auth-service exposes only 7 aggregate metrics (cpu_pct, error_rate, latency_p99_ms, memory_pct, rate_limited_per_min, request_rate, restarts) — the metric surface has no per-pod/replica/AZ label or dimension.

No per-AZ or per-replica service identifier exists: queries for 'auth-service-us-east-1a', 'auth-service-us-east-1b', 'auth-service-us-east-1c' all returned not_found, and the known_services list contains only 18 flat top-level service names, none suffixed by zone or replica index.

Pod-index style service ids do not exist either: 'auth-service-0' and 'auth-service-pod-1' both returned not_found (retried, attempts 2), with the same 18-name known_services list — so there is no per-pod dimension under any naming convention tried.

The re-attempted aggregate auth-service error_rate over 12:00-15:59Z confirms the step: flat ~0.20-0.26% avg through 13:55Z (e.g. 13:55 avg 0.26), then 14:00Z avg 22.21 (max 38.34) and a stable ~36% plateau to 15:55Z (35.99, 36.27); summary max 40.33, mean 17.89, missing_points 0 — i.e. the aggregate series is complete and the onset is unambiguous at 14:00Z.

Request volume stayed flat across the whole 12:00-15:59Z window (summary mean 398.82, min 357.99, max 435.3; 14:00Z avg 401.35, 15:55Z avg 405.81), so the aggregate error-rate step is not a traffic artefact.

The per-replica breakdown requested by T4 is not obtainable from the metric surface: the metric backend exposes only aggregate per-service series, so the subset-of-replicas vs even-spread discriminator between H2 (key rotation) and H1 (parser) cannot be resolved with metrics alone.

redis-cache hit ratio was flat and healthy across the 14:00Z onset: ~95-97% in every 6-min bucket from 13:00Z to 15:00Z (13:54 avg 96.07, 14:00 avg 96.17, 14:36 avg 96.54, 15:00 avg 95.24; summary mean 95.91, min 94.23, max 97.93, missing_points 0). There is no cache-miss/hit-ratio drop that could explain ~36% of token validations failing.

redis-cache connection pool was not saturated at onset: connected_clients stayed ~300-320 throughout (13:00 avg 306.27, 14:00 avg 310.51, 14:24 avg 313.31, 15:00 avg 324.06; summary mean 308.54, min 273.75, max 340.71, missing_points 0) with no ramp or ceiling behaviour at 14:00Z.

redis-cache evictions were low and unchanging: ~3 keys/min in every bucket (13:00 avg 2.67, 14:00 avg 3.26, 14:06 avg 3.72, 15:00 avg 2.41; summary mean 3.03, min 1.48, max 4.97, missing_points 0). Key eviction pressure (which would drop session/token entries) is absent.

redis-cache CPU was flat and far from saturation across onset: ~21-23% all window (13:00 avg 21.34, 14:00 avg 21.71, 14:36 avg 22.23, 15:00 avg 20.9; summary mean 21.94, min 19.57, max 23.99, missing_points 0). No compute pressure on the shared cache at 14:00Z.

redis-cache memory was stable, not climbing or at OOM boundary across onset: ~66-72% (13:00 avg 67.89, 14:00 avg 70.07, 14:24 avg 72.03, 14:30 avg 66.6, 15:00 avg 65.89; summary mean 69.14, min 60.31, max 77.21, missing_points 0). No memory-exhaustion event accompanies the 401 onset.

redis-cache has no error_rate or latency metric defined at all — only connected_clients, cpu_pct, evictions_per_min, hit_ratio_pct, memory_pct — so the cache's own error rate/latency cannot be read directly; however all five exposed health metrics are flat across the 14:00Z step change (hit ratio, clients, evictions, CPU, memory all unchanged), which positively excludes a shared-cache subset fault (H3) on the cache side.

dep-5710 is a single deployment record for auth-service: v7.3.0 at 2026-04-15T14:00:00Z, author d.verma, status 'live', rolled_back_at null. The record exposes no replica count, no rollout strategy (rolling/blue-green/staged) and no per-pod timing fields.

findings.statement: cfg-2705 is the only auth-service config change and it records a single scalar key update (jwt.signing.key_id 'k-2025-10' -> 'k-2026-04') at 2026-04-15T14:01:00Z by 'security-automation'. The record carries no distribution/rollout metadata (no per-replica application timestamps, no channel, atomicity flag or JWKS artifact id).

A windowed query (10-minute window 14:00-14:10Z, scope 'all services') returns exactly one deployment — dep-5710 at 14:00:00Z — with no additional deploy rows at finer granularity, so there is no second rollout event or staged sub-deploy visible within the onset window.

A windowed config-change query (13:00-15:59Z, all services) returns exactly one change — cfg-2705 at 14:01:00Z — i.e. the key-id rotation appears as a single atomic config record, not a sequence of per-instance or staged writes.

The dependency graph confirms api-gateway -> auth-service (kind http) is the only inbound caller edge to auth-service, and auth-service's own outbound edges are user-db (db), redis-cache (cache) and kyc-provider (external). api-gateway hasTelemetry=true, so gateway-side telemetry is nominally available in principle, though it was not queryable in this task.

Historical precedent HIST-108 (2025-10-01, '401s after JWT signing key rotation', root_cause 'Key rotation published new key id before all pods loaded the JWKS', category config_change, resolution 'Re-published previous key; staged rotation') was retrieved with match_score 6, and HIST-109 (library upgrade clock-skew) with match_score 2. Both are leads only, not evidence about the current incident.

findings.statement: The 401/invalid_token counter on api-gateway could not be queried at all in this task: the only telemetry path available (observability service metrics) accepted only auth-service, so api-gateway's 401 counters and error_rate were never obtained.

api-gateway deployment history was unavailable: get_deployments for api-gateway returned 'backend unavailable (503) (gave up after 3 attempts)' on every attempt (tc-050, tc-058), while the same tool succeeded for auth-service (tc-060) and a windowed all-services config query succeeded (tc-059).

api-gateway had zero config changes on 2026-04-15: get_config_changes scope api-gateway returned count 0, and the all-services query 12:00-15:59Z returned exactly one change, cfg-2705 on auth-service (jwt.signing.key_id 'k-2025-10' -> 'k-2026-04' at 14:01Z).

api-gateway is a plain edge fan-out caller of five services and is shared:false — edges api-gateway -> auth-service, order-service, portfolio-service, market-data-service, payment-service (all http) — so its 401s would be a pass-through of downstream auth-service rejections rather than a gateway-owned dependency fault.

The counter that would ground or falsify the 'callers surface 401s as logged-out sessions' final hop remains unmeasured: no gateway-side 401, error_rate or session-invalidation series was obtained, so the lockstep comparison against auth-service's 14:00Z step (~0.2% -> ~36% plateau) cannot be made from this task's data.

Notably its own 11:35Z deploy (v5.0.3) produced no error elevation in this window either.

Latency for all three co-tenants was also flat across onset, confirming they were not under any stress: portfolio-service p99 ~175-186ms (13:54 avg 183.53, 14:00 avg 176.73, 15:00 avg 181.66; mean 180.1), pricing-engine p99 ~59-62ms (13:54 avg 60.42, 14:00 avg 59.6, 15:00 avg 62.18; mean 59.68), market-data-service p99 ~40ms (13:54 avg 40.34, 14:00 avg 40.05, 15:00 avg 41.92; mean 40.13). All three summaries show missing_points 0.

All three redis-cache co-tenants expose the same generic service metric set (error_rate, latency_p99_ms, cpu_pct, memory_pct, request_rate, restarts), and portfolio-service additionally exposes db_pool_in_use. None of the three exposes a redis/cache-specific metric, so their health as cache consumers can only be read indirectly via their own service error_rate/latency.

The cross-consumer discriminator resolves as FLAT: not one of the three shared redis-cache consumers (portfolio-service, pricing-engine, market-data-service) shows any error or latency step at auth-service's 14:00Z onset. Since the shared cache they co-depend on also showed all five of its health metrics flat (team F25-F30), the failure is not propagated through the shared redis-cache, and the ~36% error elevation is confined to auth-service alone - independently hardening the H3 exclusion and the auth-service-only scope claim.
